clue.text: Place to hang hospital garment?

parts.note: a ward is a room of beds in a hospital, standing in for the whole place
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: Someone in hospital asks where they can hang up their gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'hospital garment' reads as one item but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for storing clothes on hangers is exactly a place to hang things.

clue.text: After hesitation, turned up nude, getting slap in the face

indicators.note: the nude piece comes after the hesitation piece
turned up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
in the buff means naked, so buff is nude

explanation.surface: Someone hesitated, then turned up naked and got slapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ER to RE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a blunt rejection, figuratively a slap in the face.

clue.text: Fruit is planted amid downpour

indicators.note: planted amid means put in the middle of something

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Fruit that has been planted in pouring rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Fine meadow or riverside, perhaps, for Mole!

definitions.meaning: a scenic place in the countryside
a dark mark on the skin, once thought attractive

explanation.surface: A lovely meadow or riverbank would suit Mole from The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole is the riverside character in The Wind in the Willows, but here it means a skin blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a picturesque spot in the countryside and a mark on the face thought to enhance looks.

clue.text: Reversible raincoats to take to the cleaners

indicators.note: a reversible coat can be turned inside out, so here the word for raincoats is turned back to front

parts.note: macs is short for mackintoshes, British raincoats

explanation.surface: Reversible raincoats need taking to the dry cleaners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' seems to describe the coats, but it tells you to read MACS backwards. 'Take to the cleaners' is an idiom for swindling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to the cleaners is idiom for cheating them out of money, which is to swindle or con.

clue.text: Binding agreement mysterious group's used to crush worker

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper piece sits on and crushes the one below it

parts.note: a coven is a secretive group of witches
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A shadowy group's binding pact was used to crush a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' sounds violent, but in a down clue it only means sitting on top of the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal contract or solemn pledge, a binding agreement.

clue.text: Staffing that's opposed by feminists?

definitions.meaning: the workers available for a job
read as male power, which feminists would oppose

explanation.surface: Feminists object to some staffing policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the available workforce and, split, suggests male dominance.

clue.text: Light meal the French originally shelled out for

definitions.text: Light meal the French originally shelled out for

parts.words: Light meal the French originally shelled out for
parts.note: a dish named by the French for which eggs are cracked and their shells discarded

explanation.surface: A cheap meal the French first paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled out' looks like paying money, but means eggs having their shells removed; 'the French originally' says the dish's name came from France.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light dish of beaten eggs, the eggs shelled before cooking.

clue.text: Bar runner from club with pain needing treatment

indicators.note: letters that need treatment are worked on and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A clubber in pain needs medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing treatment' rearranges CLUB and PAIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord who runs a pub runs a bar, so is a bar runner.

clue.text: Rugby player that's employed in theatre

definitions.meaning: a forward in the front row of the scrum
an object used on stage by actors

explanation.surface: A rugby player who also works in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a front-row forward in rugby and an item handled on stage.

clue.text: Drive to find area next to concert hall maybe

parts.note: a concert hall is one example of a venue

explanation.surface: Directions for finding parking near a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' just puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and avenue are both names for a road, often a tree-lined one.

clue.text: Very loud penetrating poet is sadly on the wrong track …

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the loud letters go inside the rearranged words
sadly means badly, so the letters of poet is are rearranged

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A poet's shrill reading has sadly lost its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges POET IS into OPISTE; 'penetrating' puts FF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-piste skiing is away from the prepared runs, so figuratively off course or astray.

clue.text: … hence, having no beginning or end, poem causes scramble

indicators.note: with no first or last letter, only the central letters of hence are kept

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem, cut short at both ends, causes confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a message is to put it into code so outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: Makes tracks in advance of drunken rep's order to come round clubs

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the club
drunken means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A drunken sales rep orders a round of drinks at the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' shuffles the apostrophe-less letters of rep's together with order; 'to come round' wraps that around the clubs letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To prerecord is to tape music or a broadcast beforehand, making tracks ahead of time.

clue.text: Severe forecast — ring entrepreneurs for clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping, so the words wrap the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A weather forecast tells entrepreneurs to ring round about clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is harsh and biting, so severe is a synonym.

clue.text: Row of homes?

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a quarrel within a household
the adjective meaning belonging to the home or household

explanation.surface: A line of houses along a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a terrace of houses, but it rhymes with cow here: a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a family quarrel and, as an adjective, means relating to the household.

clue.text: Food supplement put team on course

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a side is a team
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A nutritional supplement is supposed to put the team on course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link word; 'on' sets SIDE above DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: An accompanying dish of vegetables or salad supplements the main food.

clue.text: Butcher cutting son causes hysterics?

indicators.note: cutting means removing, so the son letter is dropped

parts.note: to butcher is to slaughter

explanation.surface: A butcher slicing up meat leaves his son in hysterics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' removes S from SLAUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics can mean fits of uncontrollable mirth, so the question mark flags a sense of merriment.

clue.text: One relays creepy messages of courses in Paris and Berlin by management

parts.note: 'of course' or yes in French is oui
the yes of Berlin is the German ja
a company's board is its management

explanation.surface: Messages sent between Paris and Berlin by managers seem oddly sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' stands for 'of course' meaning yes: OUI in French and JA in German.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance board with letters supposedly spells out messages from spirits, which is creepy.

clue.text: Club's number one in part of India — tall story!

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a tall story is an untruth, a lie

explanation.surface: A club's top man is said to come from India, which is a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club's number one' suggests the letter C, but it is the definition: the No. 1 shirt in football.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the keeper traditionally wears the number one shirt.

clue.text: Man whose limit may be one across and two down?

definitions.text: Man whose limit may be one across and two down?

parts.words: Man whose limit may be one across and two down?
parts.note: a chess piece (man) moves in an L shape, one square sideways and two forward or back

explanation.surface: Someone whose limit is solving one clue across and two down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one across and two down' look like crossword references, but describe a chess move.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess piece is restricted to an L-shaped hop, such as one square across and two down.

clue.text: Present that bloke goes on about

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: he refers to that man
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A present that some man keeps talking about.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be in this place, attending.

clue.text: Drive home's ending?

parts.note: the last letter of home is E, which is the physics symbol standing for the answer

explanation.surface: Someone driving home asks where the trip ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'home' is E, and E is the standard scientific symbol for this quantity: a cryptic hint rather than wordplay that builds letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means vigour and get-up-and-go, the same as vitality or force.

clue.text: Beg surgeon for facelift, having caught cold

indicators.note: having caught means holding something inside
a facelift changes the look of something, so the letters of surgeon are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A patient pleads with a surgeon for a facelift while suffering a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facelift' rearranges SURGEON; 'having caught' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to cadge things from others, a casual way to beg.

clue.text: Bothered to take time for seconds, resulting in round figure

indicators.note: take one letter in place of another, signalling a swap
for means instead of, naming which letter is replaced

parts.note: shirty is British slang for annoyed or bothered

explanation.surface: Annoyed at being made to take extra time over the seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIRTY is informal British for irritable; swapping its S for T gives the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A number ending in zero is a round number, so thirty is a round figure.

clue.text: Villain receiving old-fashioned look after page's introduction

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a rogue is a villain
lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A villain gives an old-fashioned look after a page boy introduces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' looks like part of 'page's introduction' meaning a first letter, but it is the definition; 'after' puts P before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section of a play or book, its introduction.

clue.text: Animal pelt

definitions.meaning: a long-eared mammal like a large rabbit
to pelt is to run very fast

explanation.surface: Animal pelt
explanation.definitionFit: One word names a fast-running mammal and, as a verb, to rush along, which is pelting.

clue.text: Risky material, 'First Love' penned by idiot

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the first words go inside the idiot

parts.note: an ass is a fool
best means first or top
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An idiot writes a romance called First Love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral used in insulation causes lung disease, so it is a hazardous material.
